content.text: I reviewed every input file, all ten draft sections, the numeral ledger, and all four figure briefs, and built a limitation-by-limitation ledger against the disclosure.

input.summary: Full source ledger built and traced. Every limitation of claims 1-16 (independent apparatus claim 1 and method claim 11 plus dependents 2-10 and 12-16) was matched to an exact affirmative passage of input/disclosure.md: the branch limit lower than the sum of connector ratings, per-channel contactor/connector current sensor/control-pilot interface/local connector identifier, upstream branch current sensor, isolated local bus to interfaces and contactors, the stored authorization/requested current/minimum sustaining current/energy-deficit values, the per-interval subtraction of measured non-charging branch load and configurable safety reserve, sustaining-first then deficit distribution, pilot sending and connector-sensor verification, the reduced pilot command with verification interval followed by one-at-a-time ordered shedding until branch current is below the limit ("If measured branch current remains above the branch limit after a reduced pilot command for a verification interval, the controller opens connector contactors one at a time in a stored shedding order until measured branch current is below the branch limit"), the three reclosure conditions including the randomized recovery delay, welded-contactor recording above a leakage threshold with inhibition of the other contactors on the branch and the local fault indicator, network interface with signed local authorization token and last accepted branch limit in nonvolatile memory, outage continuation and the new-session token/expiry gate, tamper-evident meter sequence uploaded on return, and the service-input one-pilot-transition-at-a-time mapping stored only after the sensed channel agrees. All 25 numerals (100, 102, 104, 106, 108, 110, 112, 114, 116, 118, 120, 122, 124, 126, 128, 130, 140, 202-216) were checked: each appears in the ledger, in at least one figure brief, and in the detailed description, with consistent part names across ledger, briefs, Brief Description of the Drawings and description, and no numeral is orphaned or duplicated across differing parts except the one distributive use of 124 reported below. All four figure briefs were checked for substantive geometry: the upstream position of branch current sensor 104 relative to all three drops, the parallel drops, the contactor-then-sensor-then-connector series order in FIG. 2, the separate dashed sensing runs versus the solid isolated local bus, the internal blocks and external fault indicator in FIG. 3, and the eight-shape FIG. 4 flow with its two decision diamonds, welded-condition terminator and two return paths, all trace to affirmative disclosure passages; the enclosure rectangles, block/circle/diamond outlines, rounded vehicle outline, equal block sizes and page placements are shape-neutral depiction conventions expressly marked "shown schematically", and no undisclosed depth, taper, angle, runout, seal, port or contact-topology statement appears. The application text contains no "by way of example", "any closed outline" or other embodiment-broadening sentence added to justify a renderer choice, and no drafting note, placeholder, open question, instruction, unresolved alternative or internal comment remains anywhere in the ten draft sections. Formalities match input/brief.md: no priority claim (cross-reference "Not applicable"), no federally sponsored research ("Not applicable"), single applicant/inventor, statutory apparatus and method classes, and no means-plus-function language. Background prior-art characterizations were not traced to the inventor, as instructed. One minor internal-consistency defect is reported; no unsupported technical assertion was found.

findings.title: Numeral 124 used distributively for the sensor of every connector channel after being assigned to the sensor of first connector channel 120
findings.detail: Numeral 124 is introduced and defined in the FIG. 2 discussion as the connector current sensor of the first connector channel 120 ("A connector current sensor 124 is arranged to measure a connector current delivered through the vehicle connector 128"; FIG. 2 brief lists "124 connector current sensor" within the dashed rectangle of first connector channel 120). The FIG. 3 paragraph then attaches the same numeral to the sensor of every channel, so a single numeral designates more than one distinct part. Every other generic reference in the description avoids this by writing the part unnumbered, e.g. "verifies the connector current resulting from the assigned current limit with the connector current sensor of that connector channel" at connector verification step 208 and "reads the connector current sensors of the connector channels" in the service input 114 paragraph. Numeral 124 also does not appear in the FIG. 3 numeral list, so no element of FIG. 3 carries it. This is a naming consistency defect only; the underlying coupling of the edge controller 106 to the connector current sensors is fully supported by the disclosure ("The controller sends each assigned limit through the control-pilot interface and verifies the resulting connector current with the corresponding current sensor.").
findings.evidence: Candidate: "Connections leave the edge controller 106 and lead to the isolated local bus 108, to the branch current sensor 104 and to the connector current sensor 124 of each connector channel." Conflicting assignment: "A connector current sensor 124 is arranged to measure a connector current delivered through the vehicle connector 128." (FIG. 2 paragraph, describing first connector channel 120) and figures/FIG-2.md: "124 connector current sensor: leader ends on the upper part of the circle outline straddling the horizontal run."
findings.fix: In draft/08-detailed-description.md, replace the sentence with: "Connections leave the edge controller 106 and lead to the isolated local bus 108, to the branch current sensor 104 and to the connector current sensor of each connector channel." No other change is required; the numeral ledger and figure briefs stay as they are.
